oracle.name: Sidisi, Regent of the Mire
oracle.oracle_text: {T}, Sacrifice a creature you control with mana value X other than Sidisi: Return target creature card with mana value X plus 1 from your graveyard to the battlefield. Activate only as a sorcery.

oracle.name: Tersa Lightshatter
oracle.oracle_text:
Haste
When Tersa Lightshatter enters, discard up to two cards, then draw that many cards.
Whenever Tersa Lightshatter attacks, if there are seven or more cards in your graveyard, exile a card at random from your graveyard. You may play that card this turn.

fixture_printed_x_record.oracle_text:
This creature enters with X +1/+1 counters on it.
At the beginning of combat on your turn, you may remove a +1/+1 counter from this creature. If you do, put a +1/+1 counter on each other creature you control.

obligation_map.name: Sidisi, Regent of the Mire
typed_support: existing ordered Additional and Mana clauses
outcomes: A nonmana X declaration has no generic-mana X charge. Its finite domain derives candidates from legal current graveyard target mana values through the typed affine amount, then validates each complete proposal with the shared borrowed funding world. Nonzero-only domains and holes remain exact.

Targets are announced before sacrifice. Only another eligible controlled creature with current copiable/face-down/off-stack printed-X mana value equal to declared X can pay; source, opponent and stale incarnations reject transactionally. X0 tokens are supported.

Mana and ordinary activation source costs can be paid before the external sacrifice, or the sacrifice can be paid first. Common ordered completion owns the clause; legacy eager activated additional payment is restricted to announcements without an ordered frame, including owned counter-payment resumption.

Full proposal funding includes a taxed mana child that returns the only matching sacrifice creature. The no-tax proposal cannot invent a mana window; the same child is legal at Priority before starting that proposal. Targets are not postponed until after those costs.

Native and acquired packet declarations share immutable source definitions. Exact X and target quantity survive source departure and real ability copying/retargeting; a departed and returned target incarnation fizzles. Sorcery timing, tap/sickness/control and sacrifice prohibitions remain enforced.
Raw and indexed owned branches agree after parent disposal and restore; a sibling can sacrifice a different same-value creature. The undeclared X domain is visible only to its chooser.

obligation_map.name: Tersa Lightshatter
typed_support: existing exact ExilePlayPermission and game Rng::below
outcomes: An actual attack checks the seven-card threshold both when triggering and resolving. The frozen packet controller supplies the graveyard and receives the normal play permission after source departure or control change.

Resolution selects uniformly among finite own physical graveyard cards using the owned unbiased RNG. Empty and singleton candidates consume no RNG; multiple seeds reach all seven exact cards. Queries and failed actor/actions do not advance RNG, and cloned raw/index/restore branches agree.

Only the selected actual successful new Exile incarnation receives the through-cleanup normal paid permission. A prevented move, an unrelated later exile, a fresh incarnation or expired turn gives no permission.

The permission retains ordinary mana costs, nonzero printed X, timing and land allowance. Both a real paid spell and ordinary land play succeed only through their legal action routes. Public exile reveals the result while unrelated hand cards remain private.
existing_card_obligations_outside_this_p: The ETB discard-up-to-two and actual discard-count draw maps to existing DiscardUpToDraw; no whole-card wiring is authored here.

state_contracts.declaration_and_ownership: Existing StackItem X, bound target wrappers, AdditionalCost receipt, cast-cost clause frame, owned RNG and exact exile-permission fields are reused. No second payment system or Oracle-English parsing is introduced.
state_contracts.integrated_layout_and_trace_owner: The complete-set integrator owns final common schema, trace and layout acceptance on the assembled head.

verification: All 19 final source hashes match the unchanged focused and compatibility consumers. Every process terminated before any subsequent consuming-input edit.
The 10/20 real failure and 19/20 fixture failure retain all 19 original source snapshots at their exact frozen hashes plus complete terminal native/guard reports and logs.
The final 20 focused and 101 directly affected cast, ordered cost, variable cost, acquired/retained activation, mana-continuation, exile-event and graveyard-permission cases pass.
Formatting uses rustfmt --edition2024 --config skip_children=true; git diff --check. No generated linkage was manually changed.
integration_dependencies_and_limits: Retain the narrow no-mana-component activation proposal guard until the separately owned shared final-total mana-window repair is reviewed and integrated. That repair must cover explicit0, reduced-to0 and Free costs as well as this pure tap/sacrifice route; this checkpoint does not claim to fix those inherited paths.

The shared repair must also assess the ordered active-Mana-row exception to mana_closed: paying any cost must not reopen mana abilities, while Convoke/Delve and other ordinary cost contributions remain legal. This adjacent source-level concern was sent to that owner and the integrator before this checkpoint publication; it is not claimed resolved here.

The isolated branch predates the integrated ExileLink.ability_origin field. Its one synthetic linked-return fixture literal needs ability_origin:None when integrated; no production link format is changed here.

ActivationNonmanaX currently targets a single typed ManaValueExactly rule whose AmountValue is affine in ChosenX through Fixed and Sum. Sidisi uses X+1. It does not claim arbitrary nonlinear nonmana-X declarations.

The prior synthetic counted-graveyard-exile mana-child limitation and unsupported non-TDM split-half mapping are explicitly reconciled in docs/tdm-cost-limitations-reconciliation.json; no native TDM obligation depends on either shape.

No TDM card behavior/admissions, full validator, complete-pool games or simulation-performance benchmark was run. Common assembled-engine acceptance and two independent final-head nonauthor reviews remain required.
